subject: POC — pricing paths & adaptive invoice-split options
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@vertex-robotics.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@vertex-robotics.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC billing — extension and split-invoice idea

Hi David,

Thanks again for running the POC last month — the team is seeing promising throughput improvements on small-batch inference. We have a few procurement constraints that make the straightforward 30-day timebox extension awkward: our finance team wants to split larger POCs across two invoices (50/50) to align with an existing budget line, and they also prefer milestone-based acceptance rather than a flat time extension.

Questions:
- Is Redwood able to structure a 6-week POC split into two invoices (milestone at week 3 and final at week 6)?
- If we do a split invoice, do you have a pricing concession for that arrangement or would it be the same as the quoted extension rate?
- Any impact to the reserved capacity/throughput guarantees if we convert a time extension into milestones?

I've attached the procurement template they want us to use (see SOW-vertex-draft.docx). Could you lay out 1–2 ways we can do this so I can take it back to finance ASAP?

Appreciate it — can we set a 30-minute call later today if helpful.

Best,
Alex
Director of ML Platforms
Vertex Robotics

Attachments: SOW-vertex-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@vertex-robotics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC billing — extension and split-invoice idea

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for attaching the procurement template. I chatted with Finance and CS and sketched two pragmatic paths that should map cleanly to your internal controls:

Option A — Timebox (6 weeks) with milestone invoices
- Structure: 6-week POC (same scope), invoiced in two equal parts: invoice 1 at signing, invoice 2 at week 4 (end-of-trial acceptance).
- Pricing: we can offer a 10% concession on the incremental extension portion if you commit to the milestone acceptance language in the SOW.
- Guarantees: no change to throughput targets; we will reserve the same GPU capacity for the duration.

Option B — Day/credit bundle with milestone drawdown
- Structure: Convert extension into a 800k-token credit bucket usable over 6 weeks. Bill 50% upfront, 50% on milestone.
- Pricing: standard extension rate (no additional concession), but credits allow predictable cost accounting and simpler overage handling.
- Guarantees: equivalent performance; credits do not change reserved slot behavior.

I attached a short pricing matrix (redwood_poc_pricing_options_v2.pdf) that shows the numbers and the suggested milestone language for the SOW. If your procurement prefers Net45 vs Net30, we can accommodate Net45 for the first invoice on this POC.

Next steps: if Option A looks good, I can draft the SOW amendment with the milestone acceptance clause and send it to your procurement for signature. If you want a quick sync, Marissa (CS) can join to confirm success criteria.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_poc_pricing_options_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@vertex-robotics.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: POC billing — extension and split-invoice idea

Alex / David — looping in Legal/Finance notes on the invoice-split approach. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we finalize language:

- Payment terms: we can accept Net45 on the first invoice for the POC, but final invoice will be Net30 unless a blanket Net45 PO is provided for Redwood's FY26 intake.
- Milestone acceptance: please define the acceptance criteria in the SOW appendix (examples: successful model run at X throughput and Y error rate on sample dataset). We prefer objective checkpoints rather than subjective language.
- PO / Tax: Procurement should attach a PO referencing the SOW and state tax jurisdiction for billing.

I'll prepare a short SOW amendment draft with the milestone language and the two billing scenarios highlighted. Once David confirms the option, I'll send the DocuSign PowerForm link to your procurement contact for signature.

Subject: Re: POC billing — extension and split-invoice idea

Thanks David and Kimberly — Option A with milestone invoices looks like the fastest path for us. Procurement confirmed Net45 on the first invoice and will attach the PO once we receive the SOW amendment.

Please:
- Send the SOW amendment with the acceptance checklist tonight if possible.
- We'll sign via your docusign link and route the PO back to you (procurement@vertex-robotics.com).

I'll block 30 minutes tomorrow at 2pm PT in case we need to run acceptance criteria by the engineering lead.

Cheers,
Alex
Director of ML Platforms
Vertex Robotics
